methods.assumption: Noise is independent between pixels and the image is smooth at the window scale; edges and small structures are blurred.
methods.label: Mean

parameters.help: Window side in pixels. Even values are raised to the next odd value.
parameters.label: Kernel size
parameters.name: kernel_size

methods.summary: Box average over a square window.

methods.assumption: Suited to impulse (salt-and-pepper) noise; non-linear and can flatten thin structures.
methods.label: Median

parameters.help: Window side in pixels. Even values are raised to the next odd value.
parameters.label: Kernel size
parameters.name: kernel_size

methods.assumption: Like the mean filter but with smoother weights; edges are blurred in proportion to sigma.
methods.label: Gaussian

parameters.help: Window side in pixels. Even values are raised to the next odd value.
parameters.label: Kernel size
parameters.name: kernel_size

parameters.help: Standard deviation of the Gaussian kernel in pixels. 0 lets OpenCV derive it from the kernel size.
parameters.label: Gaussian sigma
parameters.name: sigma

methods.assumption: High frequencies are noise. The sharp cutoff rings near edges and the transform assumes periodic borders.
methods.label: Frequency ideal

parameters.help: Cutoff radius as a fraction of the smaller half-dimension of the spectrum (1 = Nyquist). Must be in (0, 1).
parameters.label: FFT cutoff
parameters.name: cutoff_ratio

methods.summary: Hard cutoff low-pass in the Fourier domain.

methods.assumption: Smooth roll-off, no ringing; blurs like a spatial Gaussian under periodic borders.
methods.label: Frequency Gaussian

parameters.help: Cutoff radius as a fraction of the smaller half-dimension of the spectrum (1 = Nyquist). Must be in (0, 1).
parameters.label: FFT cutoff
parameters.name: cutoff_ratio

methods.summary: Gaussian low-pass in the Fourier domain.

methods.assumption: Intermediate roll-off between the ideal and Gaussian filters.
methods.label: Frequency Butterworth

parameters.help: Cutoff radius as a fraction of the smaller half-dimension of the spectrum (1 = Nyquist). Must be in (0, 1).
parameters.label: FFT cutoff
parameters.name: cutoff_ratio

methods.summary: Order-2 Butterworth low-pass in the Fourier domain.

methods.assumption: Noise is small compared with the edges to keep; flat regions are smoothed, but noise on an edge is not.
methods.label: Bilateral

parameters.help: Pixels whose intensity differs by much more than this barely influence each other (edges survive).
parameters.label: Intensity scale
parameters.name: bilateral_sigma_color

parameters.help: Spatial standard deviation in pixels; the window diameter is 2*ceil(3*scale)+1.
parameters.label: Spatial scale
parameters.name: bilateral_sigma_space

methods.summary: Averages only pixels that are close in space and similar in intensity.

methods.assumption: Image structures repeat; noise is independent and roughly Gaussian. The noise level is not supplied, only the strength h.
methods.label: Non-local means

parameters.help: Patch-similarity tolerance. Too small leaves noise, too large erases texture. Patch 5x5, search window 13x13 are fixed.
parameters.label: Filtering strength h
parameters.name: nlm_h

methods.reference: Buades, Coll and Morel, CVPR 2005, doi:10.1109/CVPR.2005.38
methods.summary: Averages pixels whose surrounding patches look alike, wherever they are.

methods.assumption: Noise is Gaussian and white; the image is sparse in the wavelet basis. Correlated noise is only partly removed.
methods.label: Wavelet (BayesShrink)

parameters.help: Noise standard deviation assumed by the BayesShrink thresholds. A strength control, not a measurement.
parameters.label: Assumed noise level
parameters.name: wavelet_sigma

methods.reference: Chang, Yu and Vetterli, IEEE TIP 2000, doi:10.1109/83.862633
methods.summary: Soft-thresholds wavelet coefficients, averaged over circular shifts.

samples.caution: Not a real scan: it shows how DICOM slices are read, not how real CT noise behaves.
samples.description: Two concentric discs (about 40 HU and 400 HU) on a -1000 HU background with Gaussian noise of 15 HU, drawn by code and stored as a DICOM file with a modality rescale. It is not an anatomical image and contains no patient data.
samples.label: Synthetic phantom (DICOM CT slice)
samples.provenance: Generated by backend/download_data.py in this repository.

samples.caution: An 8-bit export: original HU values and the DICOM header are not available, so scores are on the display scale. The Gaussian noise added here is a teaching device, not a model of CT noise.
samples.description: Slice 5 of scikit-image's data.brain(), a 10-slice subset of the University of North Carolina Volume Rendering Test Data Set, exported as an 8-bit PNG. The slice shows a skull with bright bone, so it is most likely a head CT slice and not an MRI: a secondary summary of the archive describes a CT cadaver head and an MR brain with the skull removed. The modality is inferred from the image and that description, not from metadata; scikit-image's own documentation does not state it.
samples.label: Head CT slice (PNG)
samples.licence: Not verified at the source: a secondary summary says the archive is public domain with a request to credit the University of North Carolina, but the archive page itself could not be read. Use for demonstration only.
samples.provenance: scikit-image sample data; the full data set is listed at https://graphics.stanford.edu/data/voldata/.

samples.caution: Has a banding artefact in the background. Included to show the filters on a non-radiological image.
samples.description: A single cell floating in saline, imaged by digital holography (scikit-image's data.cell()). It is a microscopy image, not tissue and not a radiological image.
samples.label: Cell in saline (quantitative phase image)
samples.licence: CC0 (public-domain dedication) according to the scikit-image documentation of data.cell.
